title: Compiler-Aided Correctness Checking of CUDA-Aware MPI Applications
problem: Detecting data races and correctness issues in hybrid CUDA-aware MPI applications is challenging because CUDA and MPI APIs are asynchronous and non-blocking, creating concurrency semantics that traditional single-model correctness tools cannot comprehensively handle.
motivation: Hybrid MPI + X models combining Message Passing Interface with node-level parallel programming increase complexity and introduce correctness issues critical to ensure reliability of large-scale HPC applications.
method: CuSan is an LLVM compiler extension that instruments CUDA code to track concurrency, synchronization, and memory access semantics at compile and runtime. It integrates with MUST (dynamic MPI correctness tool) and ThreadSanitizer (thread-level race detector) to provide comprehensive data race detection. The system leverages compiler instrumentation to expose CUDA semantics to existing race detection infrastructure designed for traditional parallel programs.
key_novelty: Integration of compiler-aided CUDA concurrency tracking with existing MPI and thread-level race detectors to enable comprehensive correctness checking of hybrid MPI+CUDA applications.
contributions: CuSan: LLVM compiler extension tracking CUDA concurrency, synchronization, and memory access semantics
Integration framework combining CuSan with MUST and ThreadSanitizer for hybrid application correctness verification
Evaluation demonstrating feasibility with measured overhead: 6-36× runtime, <1.8× memory across two mini-apps
Open-source release enabling community adoption and further development
limitations: Paper does not explicitly discuss limitations such as detection completeness, false positive rates, or applicability beyond the two evaluated mini-apps.
